subject: NAMO_TURN_DETECTOR_V1_MULTILINGUAL

architectural_interpretation.appropriate_role: semantic end-of-utterance/turn-transfer gate after or alongside streaming ASR
architectural_interpretation.recommended_f2_composition: acoustic VAD + streaming ASR + NAMO semantic EOU + local brain + cancellable TTS
architectural_interpretation.reason: The upstream formulation computes P(EOU|ASR text prefix); acoustic wake/presence/barge-in still require an audio-side signal.

hypothesis: Adding a semantic EOU gate to the German local-solo pipeline can reduce fixed-silence response delay and false turn cuts without adding material compute latency.
counterhypothesis: ASR partial instability, colloquial German, fillers, punctuation artifacts, or transcript lag can erase the upstream accuracy/latency advantage and make a tuned acoustic endpoint policy better end-to-end.

required_next_discriminator.dataset: German conversational prefixes including hesitations, enumerations, self-corrections, conjunction tails, and true turn endings
required_next_discriminator.dispatch_blocker: Existing self-hosted runner admission/liveness discriminator is still the active infrastructure gate; do not add duplicate queued runtime work.

notes: Upstream metrics are source claims, not F2 measurements.
The source pin is useful even while runtime execution is blocked because it defines an exact artifact and a falsifiable integration role.
No paid provider/API route is required for this candidate.
